title: A stronger point source
hook: Change source power and predict intensity.
misconception: intensity stays fixed when source power doubles.
objective: Apply I = P/(4πr²) to compare intensity when source power changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With an isotropic point source in a lossless medium at fixed distance, I = P/(4πr²). When source power doubles, intensity becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model I = P/(4πr²); scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider an isotropic point source in a lossless medium at fixed distance, with a nonzero initial result. If source power triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on intensity?
recall.why: Apply I = P/(4πr²) under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
